Cold Outreach Works Better With a Real Reason to Talk

Playbooklowob research

By Chris WellsFrom lowob RESEARCH · 28 May 2026 · 8-minute read · Revenue

Mentioning a prospect's podcast is not a reason to send a sales pitch. Better outreach starts with an observable change in the prospect's business and a problem you might solve because of it. Most buyers are not in market at any given time, and Gartner finds 67% would prefer to buy without a rep at all, so the bar for interrupting someone is high. Score each signal before you spend time on it, write from a hypothesis rather than a diagnosis, and use automation to cut research cost, not to raise send volume.

Cold outreach has developed a personalisation theatre problem. A seller mentions the prospect's university, praises a recent podcast, inserts a line about the funding round, and then sends the same irrelevant pitch that went to everyone else.

The email is personalised. The reason for the conversation is not. Buyers do not owe a response because a system proved it could scrape their biography. They respond when the message connects a real change in their business to a problem worth solving now. That is the difference between cosmetic personalisation and signal-based outbound.

Why the reason matters more than the greeting

Two facts set the bar. First, most of any market is not buying. The B2B Institute at LinkedIn, drawing on joint research with the Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, argues that about 95% of potential buyers are "out-market" at any given time, because companies replace most products and services only every few years. A generic message reaches mostly people with no reason to act.

Second, buyers increasingly prefer not to talk to sellers. Gartner's survey of 646 B2B buyers, published in March 2026, found 67% preferred a rep-free buying experience and 45% had used AI during a recent purchase. Gartner's buying-journey research found buyers spend only 17% of their buying time meeting potential suppliers. A seller's message has to earn a place in that small share.

A signal is how you find the minority with a live reason, and how you show them you noticed it.

A signal is evidence of a changing commercial condition

Product launches, market expansion, new executives and hiring can signal a change in priorities. So can a relevant integration, a shift in regulation, customer complaints, a competitor's move or repeated questions from users.

A signal matters only when it changes the probability, timing or value of a buying decision. Funding alone is weak. Funding specifically allocated to enterprise expansion, paired with hiring a head of partnerships, tells a more specific story.

Weak signalWhy it is weakStronger version
Raised a roundSays money exists, not what it is forRaised to expand into a named market, and hiring there
New executiveMost new hires change nothing you sell intoNew head of a function you serve, with a public mandate
Spoke on a podcastPersonal triviaSaid publicly that a problem you solve is a priority
Visited your pricing pageCould be a student or a competitorSeveral people from one target account visited in a week

Third-party intent data can add signals, with caveats about accuracy. Our explainer on intent data covers how far to trust it.

Build the outreach thesis before writing the email

For each account, complete four fields:

  • Observed change: what happened, with a link to the evidence.
  • Likely implication: what new pressure, opportunity or coordination problem it could create.
  • Relevant capability: how your product or service might help.
  • Credible next step: a small conversation or artefact that would be useful even if the prospect does not buy.

That produces a reason-to-talk statement: Because the company is doing X, the team may now encounter Y. We have relevant experience with Z and can offer Q as a useful next step.

Claude can help assemble evidence, compare it with your ideal customer profile and draft a hypothesis. The account owner should verify the source, test the logic and decide whether the implication is credible.

Score signals before spending time on them

Score each signal from zero to two on five dimensions:

Dimension012
RecencyOver six months oldOne to six monthsWithin the last month
RelevanceUnconnected to your problemIndirectly connectedDirectly creates the problem you solve
MagnitudeCosmetic changeAffects one teamChanges the business's direction or risk
AccessNo route to the decision ownerRoute to an influencerRoute to the owner or a warm introduction
ProofNothing relevant to showAdjacent experienceDirect, evidenced experience

Accounts scoring eight to ten receive high-effort research and direct outreach. Accounts scoring five to seven enter a lighter nurture motion. Lower-scoring accounts stay monitored rather than forced into a campaign. The time bands above are lowob's defaults; set your own to match your sales cycle.

Write from hypothesis, not certainty

Signal-based outreach can still fail if it pretends to know too much.

Do not write: "You must be struggling to manage your community after the launch."

Write: "The launch appears to have created a sharp increase in product questions across Discord and X. Teams at this stage often have trouble separating support issues from broader narrative risk. Is that showing up for you?"

The second version shows attention without claiming private knowledge. It opens a conversation instead of performing a diagnosis.

Keep the first message to four sentences: the signal, why it may matter, your relevant experience, and one low-friction question or offer.

Saw that you are expanding the product from crypto-native users into financial institutions. That transition usually changes the buying committee, proof requirements and content needed to support a sale. We have been mapping that shift across several infrastructure teams. Happy to share the institutional GTM checklist if it would be useful.

There is no fake compliment and no miniature brochure. The value of the message is the relevance of the premise.

Automation should reduce research cost while raising the threshold for contact.

Use AI to protect seller time, not buyer attention

A strong Claude workflow can monitor an approved account list, extract supported signals, score them against the ICP and prepare a research brief. It can flag missing evidence and generate several opening hypotheses.

It should not automatically send every message it can produce. When the marginal cost of outreach approaches zero, organisations are tempted to spend buyer attention carelessly. That is precisely when judgment matters more. Our piece Nothing sends without a person sets out the approval gate, and what an AI SDR can and cannot do covers the tools.

There is also a hard technical limit. Google's sender guidelines require all senders to keep the spam rate reported in Postmaster Tools below 0.3%, and recommend staying below 0.1%; Yahoo applies the same 0.3% ceiling. Since November 2025 Gmail has been ramping up enforcement, including rejecting non-compliant mail. A high-volume, low-relevance sequence can damage the reputation of the domain your invoices and customer emails also use. Our guide to email deliverability covers the setup.

lowob takeaways

  • Find a commercial signal, not trivia. A real change in the business beats a compliment about a podcast.
  • Score before you write. Recency, relevance, magnitude, access and proof decide where effort goes.
  • Write a hypothesis. Show what you noticed and ask whether it is true.
  • Raise the threshold as costs fall. Cheap drafting is a reason to send less, better, with a person approving.

Common questions

What is signal-based outbound?

It is prospecting that starts from an observable change in a target company, such as an expansion, a relevant hire or a regulatory shift, and contacts the company only when that change makes your offer timely. The message is built around the signal.

What are examples of buying signals in B2B?

Strong signals include a funded expansion into a market you serve, a new leader of a function you sell to, a public statement that your problem is a priority, a relevant regulatory change, or several people from one target account researching your category.

Does personalising cold emails improve response rates?

Personalising the greeting does little if the reason for writing is generic. What helps is a specific, verified reason the message is relevant now, stated as a hypothesis the reader can confirm or reject.

Can AI write and send cold emails automatically?

It can draft and research well, but sending without review risks spam complaints, inaccurate claims and domain damage. Google and Yahoo cap spam rates at 0.3%. Keep a person approving each send.
